title: Riftlight review (Nov 6): the runs, what the agents said, a light look at the games, the plans then and now, and home's GPT runs
summary:
**28 finished Riftlight builds and 7 plans.** 20 builds are Claude's. 8 are from other models in the first batch, and all of those are flagged with `*` in Results. RegrettableEvil4 (Opus xhigh) was still going at 18 hours, so it isn't counted.

**In short:** all 28 games load, run and make sound, and 26 of the 28 agents say the whole-game bot was their most helpful test. Claude's and GPT Sol's builds all look like real games in this light look, with one visible bug. Grok's and Muse's are rougher. Agents' top engine requests repeat: errors that fail silently, per-pad input, a menu layer and proper camera rigs.

**What this was:** I read every result and exit interview, then opened each game on the graphics card. I watched its demo, pressed through its menus and gave it crude input. **Nobody played these games properly, me included,** so this says nothing about feel or how they play past the first minutes.

**Also here:** the HOME findings cover the GPT Sol runs on your home computer, as pushed by 07:33 on Nov 6 (commit a91c8b4). More runs are still coming, so those are a snapshot. Six agents reviewed that branch from a separate copy, three reading and three checking, and I verified the points below that you'd act on. Nothing was merged.

findings.title: WhyFit shows a GAME ERROR banner to the player if a key is pressed during part of its demo
findings.found:
Let the demo run, press a key while it's showing the island, and a purple banner appears: `GAME ERROR: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'day')`. It stays on screen for the rest of the session, over the title and into the game. The game still works underneath it.

It happened at 9 of 13 press times tried: every one from 12 to 23 s, plus 44 and 55 s; not at 5, 26, 30 or 36 s.

**Cause:** leaving the demo clears the player's save slot (`stopAttract` in `src/app.js`), but the island scene draws once more before the title loads, and reads `S.day` from the empty slot. A fresh player has no save, so they're the ones who hit it.

**Also once:** in one late press the demo kept playing for 20 s through four key presses. I couldn't repeat that in two further tries.
findings.did: Not fixed: this is a finished run's game. It would be a one-line guard in `HubScene.draw`. Its agent couldn't have seen it through the game check, because the check doesn't press anything (GAME-2).
findings.check: Fresh page per try, one key press at a set time. The stack names `HubScene.draw`.

findings.title: The Claude and Sol builds all look like real games, and Grok and Muse are rougher
findings.found:
Claude's 19 builds besides WhyFit, and all 3 of Sol's, look finished in these moments: clean menus, readable text, and a demo showing real play. On this look I can't separate Sonnet from Opus, except that FarPry2 is the weakest. The longest builds don't look better than the shortest: TollBoothOfDoom (11.4 h) against Diabellical (2.8 h), FarDrySeason (16.1 h) against FarCryUncle (7.2 h). That's presentation only, not depth, balance or feel.

Strongest first impressions: FarCryUncle, Trauma Ward (Sol), WeFitIn, HonkIfYouOwe, GranTumbleweed, Diabellical.

Rougher:
- **Fit-Getaway (Muse, 0.3 h):** text overlapping the scale, and grey boxes that look like debug drawing.
- **Mint-Dial (Grok):** text across the characters, with low contrast.
- **A Cry Too Far (Grok):** flat and sparse (GAME-4).
- **The Second Opinion Clinic (Grok):** a flat surgical field, and PRESS hidden behind the figures.
- **A Little Off Balance (Terra):** clean, but it looks like a web app, not the engine's pixel look. Terra compacted 65 times in that build ([Codex catalog gap, Nov 5]), so don't judge the model by it.

findings.title: A "Reconnecting" message labels finished GPT runs as failed, and Retry failed would delete them
findings.found:
The runner marks a run failed on any `error` event in Codex's stream. Codex sends those while reconnecting, even when it then falls back to HTTPS and finishes. These 5 Sol builds here all exit 0, reach `turn.completed`, and have a game and an interview, but they're labelled failed:

- `x54facc` my-3dge, Wii Fit
- `x29b4d9` tech-v5, Wii Fit
- `x24ebb3` riftlight, Trauma Center (Trauma Ward)
- `xc21248` tech-v5, Far Cry 2
- `xd6caf5` my-3d2dge-v3, Diablo 3

5 more at home are the same: 4 max and 1 ultra.

**The risk:** Retry failed is on in the live batch, and GPT is on hold. A retried run deletes its old folder when the new name differs, and names carry the start time. So lifting GPT's hold with Retry on would delete those 5 games and pay to rebuild them.
findings.did: Nothing changed. Turn Retry failed off before lifting the hold. The real fix is to count a run as failed only on `turn.failed` or a non-zero exit, and that's a repo change for you to call.
findings.check: Read each log's end and the code: `isDone` treats only status ok as done, and the folder is removed on retry.

findings.title: Home's GPT runs: high completion holds, but 24 at once lasted 44 minutes before memory ran short
findings.found:
| Stage and effort | Runs | Labelled OK | Median minutes |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-shot, max | 47 | 39 | 53 |
| One-shot, ultra | 51 | 50 | 30 |
| Plan, ultra | 22 | 22 | 15.5 |
| Build, max | 21 | 21 | 93.5 |
| Build, ultra | 20 | 20 | 51 |

**Completion:** 152 of 161 are labelled OK (94.4%). All 157 that started reached their end. 4 never started, because the environment file was missing, and 5 are false failures (HOME-2).

**Not in those numbers:** the PC's sleep cut off 16 runs, which started over. 6 planned one-shots have no record, because a stopped run's folder is deleted, so the cause is unknown. 3 builds were held back by the pause.

**24 at once:** one stretch, 19:14 to 19:58, all one-shot max. Home's own commit says "Parallel runs lowered to 16 at about 19:50, when memory ran short", and the next batch ran "16 at a time". So 16 was the working level on 16 GB. Ultra and the builds never went above 16. Logs from the 24 stretch show a run seeing 1.2 GB available with all 8 GB of swap used, and some browsers dying or hanging, though nothing proves a memory kill. No memory log came from home.

**No spiralling:** 0 compactions in 157 runs, and about $700 of tokens at list price.

**Quality is unmeasured.** The game check ran on 96, all clean, and was skipped on 39. 48 of the 55 one-shot check screenshots are mostly white. In the 6 opened, the score and timers are live over a blank 3D picture. That's the game check's flags (PROMPT-2), not broken games, and #37 fixes it for checks from now on. Nobody has seen these games run.

findings.title: Why GPT builds are shorter: mostly no goal check, and it doesn't sit waiting on tests
findings.found:
Compared on this computer, on the same plans and engines:

- **No goal check:** Sol's prompt has no "Done when", so nothing ever sends it back. Where Claude's goal settled within 2 checks, Claude took 1.08 times as long as Sol. With more checks, 2.29 times. Against Claude's fastest build on each of 5 plans, Sol is only about 8% faster at the median.
- **Test share:** a test was going for 23% of the time on Sol's 3 Riftlight builds, 38% on Claude's builds with 2 or fewer checks, and 65% on those with more.
- **Price:** Sol's list price is 5% to 26% of Claude's (median 16.5%) on the same plans. That's list price, not what you paid.
- **Test wording isn't it:** `test-tools-v2` and `v3` differ by one sentence about subagents.

**Memory follows what's being tested more than how many runs are going.** Real earlyoom kills here: 1 on Sep 30, 5 on Oct 10, and 318 on Nov 5. There were none with 57 runs at once on Oct 29, and none with 24 Claude builds on the 2D engine on Nov 4. So the RAM should help, but software WebGPU testing and `/tmp` were the cause, not the count alone.

**Max per model:** home ran up to 24 of one model with no "at capacity" errors, while here 2 such failures came with only 4 or 5 Sol running. So the cap of 3 here may be stricter than it needs to be. One night isn't proof.

Model, Codex and the missing goal check always change together, and builds that pass early may simply be easier ones, so none of this is a clean test. It says nothing about which games are better.
findings.did: No action. Your call on Nov 6 was that testing is fine when it's productive.
findings.check: Same-plan pairs from result.json, plus timing from 9 Sol session logs on this computer. Home's logs have no timestamps, so its own test share is only estimated.

findings.found:
`dashboard.mjs` and `dashboard.html` are unchanged on this branch, so any page edits you made at home haven't been pushed. All 101 Node tests pass on it. No browser tests were run.

| Commit | What | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|

**Why not the config:** this computer's next Start would plan 8,343 GPT runs, a Claude pick would fail, the Claude Test buttons wouldn't find their models, and the reports would relabel 386 older runs. The running batch is safe either way, because it uses its own copy.

**How:** the commits touch separate files, so they can be taken one at a time. A plain fast-forward is refused today, because `runs/index.html`, `runs/prompt-history.json` and `runs/results.csv` have local changes here. New runner code applies to the next batch, and "Restart once it has finished" avoids cutting a build off.

**Two older bugs the review found, also on main:** Preview fails on a very big queue because the dry run's output gets cut short (`run-matrix.mjs:760`), and through the dashboard a next plan can start before a finished plan's builds. A small patch closed both in a scratch copy. It isn't applied anywhere.

findings.title: Riftlight fails silently on wrong names: the worst bugs in several runs
findings.found: A wrong ease name in a clip, or `sawtooth` for the wave `saw`, gives NaN with no error. `validateClip` and `analyzeClip` both stay silent. 6 of 28 agents hit this. It cost them invisible avatars, every custom animation at once, or total silence through the master bus. One called it "the worst bug of the run". A NaN pose can also end in a bare Rapier `unreachable` panic: 6 agents mention Rapier crashes, and one never found the cause and replaced Breakables instead.

Goal-met rates barely moved: Opus xhigh 56% to 56%, Opus medium 32% to 33%, Sonnet 12% to 8%. The 15 queued `my-3d2dge` builds should give the first fair comparison.

That's what they were told to do: builders had `TASK.md`, so nothing was lost then. Without it, those are what a builder would miss.

**The engine's link, corrected Nov 6.** An exact link isn't needed if the plan gives what the builder needs. **Did it cause problems? No.** All 34 Claude builds read `TASK.md`, and all 32 whose engine has a link fetched the engine from it. Only 2 of their 136 prompt-feedback answers mention anything like this, and neither is about the engine. It would only have mattered without `TASK.md`, which is the new setup.

| The game check's 6 | Run, but the 3D picture is blank in a screenshot | about 0.2 s |

Agents are now told the 5, and to use them only for WebGPU games, in place of the old note that a WebGPU canvas can come out blank. The game check checks every game as before, then takes a WebGPU game's screenshot from a second browser with the 5, which adds up to about 45 s or more per WebGPU game. A test keeps the two lists the same. my-3dge is so slow in software that its screenshot can still catch its Loading screen. findings.title: Planners want to know who builds and how big, and the file-name rule contradicts the goal
findings.found:
- 23 of 27 want to know which models build it, or on what budget.
- 21 want to know which lines are for the planner and which for the builder.
- 20 want a target length.
- 13 of 28 builders agree in their own answers, asking for a ranked minimum or a cut list.

**A contradiction:** the plan stage says to leave out `TASK.md`'s file names, and the goal says "covers everything TASK.md asks for". At least 2 of the 4 plans forced past their goal check failed on exactly that.
findings.did:
**Fixed Nov 6 in #37 and #38,** from your answers. The Build tab only points at `PLAN.md`: "Build the game PLAN.md describes", the model, effort and stamp for its file names, which a plan can't know, and the `PROGRESS.md` line. A stage's runs get `TASK.md` only if its text or goal names it. `plan-v4` says `PLAN.md` is the only thing the builders get and they build all of it, and its goal takes file names as patterns, which ends the contradiction. The budget is in the Stage 1 prompt: assume it's unlimited, and don't let it influence the work.

**Left out, as you decided:** a target length, because the planner decides how much is built and the builders build it. Who builds isn't named either. Home's `plan-v3` does that in one sentence, if you want it.

**One thing to watch:** a plan now carries its computer's notes, so a plan made here and built at home has this computer's.
